svg.title: Unsaved changes on close, leaving for an agent's page, and replacing changed agents when switching template
svg.desc: A: Edit team on Docs with changes; Esc or Close turns the panel footer into the question Discard your changes to Docs, with Keep editing focused and Discard. B: the same question when following Open drafter's page, worded Discard and open. C: New team copying Writing with three changed agents; picking Research in the template select asks in place under Start from: Replace your 3 changed agents with Research's, Keep mine focused and Replace. Light theme, existing tokens.
svg.text: Unsaved changes and replacing a template
Every question is asked in place, on the safe answer first; no second dialog over the panel. Words from copy.md.
A · ESC OR CLOSE, WITH CHANGES (EDIT TEAM ON DOCS)
Edit the Docs team
… the body, unchanged: drafter "edited", researcher "will be removed when you save", critic "new" …
drafter
was writer
edited
Discard your changes to Docs?
The team renamed, 1 agent changed, 1 added
and 1 removed. They aren't saved.
Keep editing
Discard
1 · The footer becomes the question
Esc, Close (×) or a click on the scrim with changes: the footer's actions are replaced by the question, as Remove
team's confirm does, and focus moves to Keep editing. The footer is a group named by the question, so a
screen reader hears it. Esc again, or Keep editing, puts the footer back and focus where it was. Discard
closes without saving; focus returns to the button that opened the panel. With no changes, all three close at
once. The second line counts edited, added and removed agents apart. New team: "Discard this new team?".
"Changed" means differs from what was loaded (or copied): typing a change back undoes it.
Leaving the page
A link elsewhere in the app (the sidebar is behind the scrim, so only links inside the panel, such as a task) asks
the same question with "Discard and open"; reload or closing the tab gets the browser's own beforeunload prompt.
Browser Back and the phone's back gesture ask this question in the footer (states-url.svg F).
B · "OPEN DRAFTER'S PAGE" WITH CHANGES
drafter
… its fields …
Knowledge, where it runs and a taller prompt editor:
Open drafter's page
Open drafter's page and discard your changes?
Save first to keep them; the page shows what is saved.
Keep editing
Discard and open
2 · Same question, saying where you'd go
The link is a real link (/agents/drafter), so with no changes it simply goes there and the panel closes; with
changes it asks first, in the footer. drafter's page is reached by its saved name: a renamed, unsaved agent's
link goes to its old name's page. A new, unsaved agent has no page: its row shows the New team line instead
("Knowledge and where it runs: on its own page, once you save.").
Opening in a new tab (middle click, Ctrl+click) doesn't ask: nothing is lost.
C · NEW TEAM: PICKING RESEARCH AFTER CHANGING THREE OF WRITING'S AGENTS
Start from
Blank
Copy a template
Research
Replace your 3 changed agents with Research's?
Research's 4 agents replace Writing's; your changes to writer, researcher and fact-checker go.
Keep mine
Replace
… the rows below stay as they are, and editable, until you answer …
Agents · one coordinates
… editor, writer "edited", researcher "edited", fact-checker "edited" …
3 · Ask before replacing, in place under the control
Shown only when rows differ from the template they were copied from (edited, added or removed). With no
changes, picking another template, or Blank, replaces the rows at once. Focus moves to Keep mine.
Keep mine (or Esc) puts the select back to Writing, the question goes, and focus returns to the select.
Replace fills the rows from Research (names numbered where taken), closes them all, and focus returns
to the select; a polite live region says "Replaced with Research's 4 agents".
Team name: if it still holds the old template's suggestion ("Writing 2"), it follows ("Research 2");
a name you typed is kept.
Switching to Blank
The same question: "Replace your 3 changed agents with a blank team?" (Blank leaves one
coordinator row). The segmented control shows the pending choice until you answer.
Why not undo instead of asking
An undo would need the whole set of rows kept and a place to offer it; replacing is rare and costly to
redo by hand, so one question is the cheaper, clearer guard. Removing a single agent keeps its Undo stub.
